providers.title: Regular points
providers.scope: At a regular point of a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field, the derivation module is free of rank equal to the dimension, also after a principal localization.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A counterexample in characteristic p
providers.scope: k[x,y,z]/(xy - z^p) in characteristic p is a normal domain of dimension two, singular at the origin, with free derivation module on x d/dx - y d/dy and d/dz.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Every dimension
providers.scope: Adjoining variables to a two-dimensional counterexample gives normal domains of every dimension n+2 with free derivation module and nonregular locus of codimension two.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Adjunction on the quadric
providers.scope: For a smooth curve of bidegree (c,d) on P^1 x P^1, the residue gives an isomorphism of O(c-2,d-2) restricted to the curve with its canonical bundle, with explicit chart formulas.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Switches and torsion
providers.scope: On a smooth (2,2) curve, the composite T of the two switches satisfies O(T(p) - p) = S - F, and k(S - F) is trivial exactly when T^k(p) = p.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: An explicit elliptic curve with a point of order four
providers.scope: The smooth (2,2) curve through the eight-point zigzag on the grid {0,1,2,3}^2 has S - F of exact order four.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The quadratic form
providers.scope: A unique element of Sym^2 of the sections of Phi multiplies to -eta/omega; its quadratic form is nondegenerate, isotropic exactly at the ramification points of the first projection.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Six vectors
providers.scope: In a nondegenerate quadratic plane: six nonzero vectors in three distinct nonisotropic directions, avoiding a finite set, with w^2 = 90 and w_j^2 + w_j.w = 1 for their sum w.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A curve of genus 21 with fourth-order contact
providers.scope: A smooth curve of bidegree (8,4), of genus 21, meets the elliptic curve exactly at the six points, with contact of order exactly four; smoothness by a dimension count, without Bertini's theorem.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Adjoint jets
providers.scope: Evaluation of adjoint sections on the subschemes of length at most four at the marked points has the same rank on the curve of genus 21 as on the elliptic curve; table of ranks 6, 12, 12, 10.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The curve data
providers.scope: Genus 21, deg L = 10, 4L = K, section dimensions h^0(L) = 2, h^0(2L) = 3, h^0(Z) = 1, h^0(2L+H) = 6, and surjective evaluation of (k+1)L on the marked points for k >= 2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The residue theorem
providers.scope: The residues of a meromorphic differential on a smooth projective curve sum to zero; proved through the trace to P^1 and partial fractions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Realizable principal parts
providers.scope: Principal parts along an effective divisor are realized by a global section exactly when they annihilate the jets of all sections of K - B under the residue pairing.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Grothendieck's splitting theorem
providers.scope: Every vector bundle on P^1 is a direct sum of line bundles O(a_i), with the integers a_i determined by the bundle.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A perfect trace pairing
providers.scope: For a finite map f: C -> P^1 and 2Lambda = K + 2H, the pairing Tr(T1 T2 / eta) on f_*Lambda is perfect and symmetric.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The trace form
providers.scope: f_*Lambda splits as O(3) + O^2 + O(-3); the trace form induces a nondegenerate form on a two-dimensional quotient W, with explicit squares of the evaluations at the marked points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Comparison with the elliptic curve
providers.scope: Principal parts along twice the marked divisor identify W with the sections of Phi on the elliptic curve; the dual map is an isometry, sign and scalar included.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The residue data
providers.scope: A pair of meromorphic sections of 2L with simple poles at the six points whose local data satisfy p(0) ^ R(0) = 1 and sum (W_j - 1) = -9 deg L.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Splitting along the marked points
providers.scope: A cocycle of sections meromorphic at the marked points splits into an algebraic outside part and holomorphic inside parts exactly when its residues against all sections of K - B vanish.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The second-order obstruction vanishes
providers.scope: The four residue tests of the order-two vertical mismatch vanish, the totals being -(3/4) epsilon_ij deg L inside and outside.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite compatible jets
providers.scope: Finitely many gluing changes of orders 1 to 7 and two vector fields matching through index seven, with wedge t^5 (1 + O(t)) d/dt ^ d/dz.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Realization
providers.scope: The gluing changes define a Hausdorff complex surface containing the curve with self-intersection -10, and the jets give sections modulo the ninth power of the ideal.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded vanishing
providers.scope: H^1 of the graded pieces of I^9 F vanishes, so H^1 of every finite quotient of I^9 F vanishes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: An analytic counterexample (assuming N1-N5)
providers.scope: A normal surface germ, singular at one point, with free derivation sheaf of rank two; resolution by a curve of genus 21 and self-intersection -10. Uses five named theorems of Grauert, Cartan and the extension theorem on normal surfaces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite determinacy with a relation matrix
providers.scope: If T^1 has finite length, equations g close to f together with an exact relation matrix close to that of f define the same complete local ring, up to an automorphism and a change of generators.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Algebraization of an isolated germ (assuming A1, A2)
providers.scope: A normal analytic germ with isolated singularity and free derivations has an affine normal algebraic model with the same completion and free derivation module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The counterexample (assuming N1-N5, A1, A2)
providers.scope: A finitely generated normal C-algebra A of dimension two with Der(A) free of rank two and a nonregular maximal ideal: the Lipman-Zariski conjecture fails in characteristic zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
